title: Bridging Structure and Function: An Integrative Characterization of Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT) for High-Performance Ferroelectric Memory
content: The increasing demand for high-speed, low-power, and non-volatile memory technologies has driven significant interest in ferroelectric materials, particularly lead zirconate titanate (PZT). As one of the most widely studied ferroelectrics, PZT exhibits robust remanent polarization and high piezoelectric coefficients, making it a prime candidate for ferroelectric random-access memory (FRAM). Unlike conventional charge-based memories, FRAM leverages the ability of PZT to switch polarization states in response to an applied electric field, offering fast switching speeds, low power consumption, and long-term data retention [1, 2]. However, scaling FRAM for commercial applications requires addressing key challenges such as fatigue, retention loss, and domain wall pinning, all of which are closely linked to the underlying material properties. A detailed understanding of the structure-property relationships in PZT is crucial for optimizing device performance and ensuring high fabrication yield.
